clue.text: A sex clue contrived about British? That can be forgiven

indicators.note: something contrived is artificially put together, so the letters before it are rearranged
about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the abbreviation that follows

blocks.note: the letters of these three words, to be rearranged
B is the standard abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: A setter apologises for a risqué clue, hoping the British will pardon it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something excusable is pardonable: a fault others are willing to overlook and let pass.

clue.text: Half open? Near – shut in

indicators.note: half tells you to keep only two of the four letters of the following word and drop the rest

blocks.note: taken as written, then cut to its back half
near and close both mean not far away

explanation.surface: A door left half open, nearly shut, with someone trapped inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To enclose something is to surround it with walls or a fence so it is confined.

clue.text: Look after exhibition of great appeal round Royal Academy

indicators.note: round means placed around, so the first word wraps the academy abbreviation

blocks.note: something cute shows great charm or appeal
RA is the usual abbreviation for the Royal Academy of Arts in London

explanation.surface: Organising a popular exhibition at the Royal Academy in London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Academy is a London art institution famous for its exhibitions, which is what makes 'look after' read as a curator's job.
explanation.definitionFit: To curate a show or collection is to select, organise and care for its items.

clue.text: His cooking includes American rice-based dish

indicators.note: cooking works ingredients into something new, so the word before it is rearranged
includes means holds within, so the rearranged letters wrap the abbreviation

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged as S and HI
US is the abbreviation for American, as in United States

explanation.surface: A man's home cooking features an American-style rice dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is a Japanese dish of vinegared rice topped or rolled with raw fish and vegetables.

clue.text: Nasty stink over a snake

indicators.note: in a down entry, over means placed above, so the first piece sits on top of the second

blocks.note: BO is body odour, an unpleasant smell
taken as written

explanation.surface: A foul smell hangs over a snake, as if it reeks.
explanation.definitionFit: A boa is a large constricting serpent of tropical America that kills prey by squeezing.

clue.text: Former boundary broken by Newton, practical scientist

indicators.note: a word broken by another is split open with that other placed in the gap

blocks.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
a perimeter is the outer boundary of an area
N is the symbol for the newton, the unit of force

explanation.surface: Isaac Newton breaks old limits as a hands-on scientist.
explanation.walkthrough: Isaac Newton fits the scientist picture, but here he is only the unit of force named after him.
explanation.definitionFit: An experimenter tests ideas through hands-on trials, the practical side of scientific work.

clue.text: Wild ox thus getting into scrap

indicators.note: getting into means entering, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: to bin something is to scrap it; this is its opening, split by the next piece
so and thus both mean in this way
the end of the same word for discard

explanation.surface: A wild ox thereby gets into a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' looks like a noun for a fight, but it is the verb meaning to throw away.
explanation.definitionFit: The bison is a large shaggy wild bovine of North America and Europe, a kind of ox.

clue.text: Sweet goat possibly getting bed in school

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the bed word sits within the school abbreviation

blocks.note: an animal that butts, as a goat does with its horns
SCH is a standard abbreviation for school
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: A cute goat gets a bed in the school, perhaps as a pet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goat possibly' is a definition by example: a goat is one kind of creature that butts.
explanation.definitionFit: Butterscotch is a hard brittle confection made from brown sugar and butter.

clue.text: Heel I allowed to get caught in street, initially tripping over

indicators.note: caught in means trapped inside, so the first words go within the street abbreviation
initially points to the opening letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: ST is the abbreviation for street
taken as written
let means allowed or permitted
the first letter of this word
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Someone in high heels trips over in the street.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six balls, abbreviated O on the scorecard.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiletto is a thin high heel on a woman's shoe, named after the slender dagger.

clue.text: Who has ace and ten, perhaps primarily hoaxing a royal pair?

definitions.text: Who has ace and ten, perhaps primarily hoaxing a royal pair?

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so take the leading letter of each following word

blocks.note: an ace and a ten are examples of playing cards
the leading letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A cheat at cards, holding a hidden ace and ten, fools someone holding a pair of kings or queens.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a card cheat is someone who holds the ace and ten and fools the player with a royal pair.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardsharp is a swindler who cheats at card games, often by secretly holding winning cards.

clue.text: Test procedure introduced by industrialists

indicators.note: introduced by means brought in by the next word, which carries the letters inside it

blocks.note: the letters run inside this word, after its first four

explanation.surface: Factory owners bring in a new testing procedure.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial is an experiment or test of performance, quality or suitability.

clue.text: Who sells clothes available in better shape

blocks.note: out means available, as a new book or film is out
fitter means healthier, in better physical condition

explanation.surface: A shop assistant offers clothes that will help you look trimmer.
explanation.definitionFit: An outfitter is a shop or trader supplying garments and equipment, especially for a particular activity.

clue.text: Shape altering in a fluid way

indicators.note: something fluid flows and changes form, so the word before it is reshaped

blocks.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A form that shifts and morphs fluidly.
explanation.definitionFit: A triangle is a plane figure with three straight sides and three angles.

clue.text: Preferably, the woman’s pursuing betrayer

indicators.note: pursuing means following behind, so the first piece comes after the second

blocks.note: a rat is an informer or traitor
her is the possessive for a woman

explanation.surface: A wronged woman would sooner chase the man who betrayed her.
explanation.definitionFit: Rather, as in 'I would rather', expresses choosing one thing over another, the sense of preferably.

clue.text: US circus showman that’s one for new element

indicators.note: one thing for another means swapping it in as a replacement

blocks.note: P. T. Barnum, the 19th-century American showman behind Barnum's circus
I is the Roman numeral one
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A famous American showman is swapped for a new act in the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Barium is a soft silvery metallic chemical element, number 56, used in X-ray imaging.

clue.text: Speak to daughter trying on a garment?

indicators.note: someone trying on clothing is inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a dress is one kind of garment
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A parent has a word with their daughter while she tries on clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: To address someone is to direct spoken words at them, as in a formal speech.

clue.text: What’s very likely to be spotted in game

definitions.text: What’s very likely to be spotted in game

blocks.clueFragment: What’s very likely to be spotted in game
blocks.note: surface reading: something easily noticed while playing, or game birds a hunter sees
setter's reading: literally covered in spots, the dotted tile used in a well-known table game

explanation.walkthrough: 'Spotted' means seen in the surface, but means marked with dots in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A domino is a small rectangular tile marked with pips, played in the game of dominoes.

clue.text: Drat this puzzle!

blocks.note: first meaning: an angry exclamation, read as two words
second meaning: the grid the solver is filling in right now

explanation.surface: A frustrated solver curses the grid they are stuck on.
explanation.walkthrough: Drat is a mild curse, which split into two words is an angry, or cross, word.
explanation.definitionFit: This very grid of clues is a word game, and an irritated exclamation is a bad-tempered utterance.

clue.text: What cleaner does in Earls Court to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent means partly, so only part of the place name is used

blocks.note: the letters straddle the two words of this place name

explanation.surface: A cleaner at work in Earls Court, a district of west London.
explanation.definitionFit: To scour is to scrub hard to remove dirt, the job of someone who cleans.

clue.text: Just fitting exactly

blocks.note: first meaning: fair and proper, morally correct
second meaning: precisely

explanation.walkthrough: 'Just fitting' looks like 'only fitting', but just means fair and fitting means suitable, both senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means morally correct or proper as an adjective, and precisely or directly as an adverb.

clue.text: Fossil commonplace around central parts of wild Gobi

indicators.note: central parts are the middle letters of each word that follows
around means surrounding, so the first word wraps the selected letters

blocks.note: trite means commonplace; this is its opening
the two middle letters of this word
the two middle letters of this word
the rest of the same word for hackneyed

explanation.surface: Fossils are common around the wild Gobi desert, famous for its finds.
explanation.definitionFit: A trilobite is an extinct marine arthropod commonly found preserved in ancient rock.

clue.text: Half and half, I’m well and not well

indicators.note: half and half means keep half of each of the two following words and lose the rest

blocks.note: taken as written: the first half of the first word and the second half of the second are kept

explanation.surface: Someone says they feel half fine and half poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill means sick or in poor health, the opposite of feeling fine.

clue.text: Pike maybe taking small fruit

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: A pike fish snapping up a little piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pike' suggests the fish; here it is the long-shafted infantry weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A pike is a long pole weapon with a pointed head, so it is one example of the thrusting weapon.

clue.text: Killing Phil, Mario and Gus? Off with their heads!

indicators.note: the Queen of Hearts' cry means remove the first letter of each of the three names

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A murderous order to execute three men, in the manner of the Queen of Hearts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Killing' looks like murder, matching the execution theme, but it is the informal adjective for extremely funny.
explanation.definitionFit: Something killing is so funny it makes you helpless with laughter, just like something uproarious.
